business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fabless Integrated Circuit Architecture and IP Core Licensing

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (Republic of South Africa) - single unitary national company registry; no sub-state incorporation distinction for private companies
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system fusing Roman-Dutch common law, English common law equity and procedural rules, and s 211-recognised African customary law, subject to the supremacy of the Constitution, 1996
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment, 2006
South Africa-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (2011, as amended by the Multilateral Instrument)
South Africa-United States Trade and Investment Framework Agreement (2012)
South Africa-People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement (2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as revised by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 26A and 56A (statutory beneficial-ownership register and filing duty to CIPC, inserted 2022); Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (assented 26 July 2024, beneficial-ownership sections pending proclamation); CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing Directive (2023); Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; FIC Guidance Notes 6 and 7 of 2023 (accountable-institution CDD and targeted financial sanctions screening).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each natural-person shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country passport-issuing authority; certification by a notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) - South Africa and the document origin state being parties; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each natural-person UBO (bank statement or utility bill issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or utility provider in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Company extract or Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction (e.g., CIPC for South African corporate shareholders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly executed power of attorney in favour of the South African incorporation agent or attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each shareholder/UBO executing before a notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the principal bank of each UBO/shareholder supporting FICA client due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the FIC Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS) list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic and international politically-exposed-person (PEP) databases, with enhanced due diligence (EDD) for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and non-face-to-face engagements under FICA s 21 and FIC Guidance Notes 6/7 of 2023; electronic identity verification with biometric liveness checks is the market standard.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC Online eServices portal of the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A name may be submitted in any of South Africa's 11 official languages but must be expressed in Latin script; it must comply with s 11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 (e.g., a surname with initials, a coined word, or a combination plus a mandatory legal-form suffix such as '(Pty) Ltd' or 'Proprietary Limited'); it must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, external company, or trade mark, and must not be offensive or falsely suggest patronage by the State.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may amend and resubmit CoR 9.1 through eServices; file a CIPC reconsideration request within 20 business days; or apply to the Companies Tribunal for a name-review order under s 160 of the Companies Act, with a subsequent appeal to the High Court. A fresh reservation application may also be filed immediately, since a rejection does not bar filing a distinctive alternative name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a fabless IP-licensing company: the Companies Act requires only a physical street address in South Africa at which statutory notices and court process may be served; a serviced registered-office (virtual office) provider satisfies the requirement provided the address is a real street address (a P.O. Box is non-compliant), the provider is contractually bound to forward process, and the company's statutory records are made available at or through that office on request.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated at under 5% per annum for a low-risk, employee-less fabless semiconductor design and IP-licensing entity; CIPC physical verifications occur mainly on complaint, insolvency, or risk-scored AMLCFT triggers, while SARS and the Department of Employment and Labour conduct targeted inspections only later in the entity's lifecycle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a single-UBO non-resident incorporation with AML file

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended), ss. 13-24 and 66; Companies Regulations 2011, Forms CoR 9.1 and CoR 14.1; Taxation Laws Amendment Act as applicable for fiscal registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), 77 Meintjies Street, Sunnyside, Pretoria; online via www.cipc.co.za e-Services portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) filed under ss. 13 and 14 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company; shares may be par-value or no-par and issued for board-determined consideration; no escrow account requirement; solvency and liquidity tests under s. 4 and s. 40 apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the incorporation of the company as a private company (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, filed with CIPC on the date of this resolution, be and is hereby ratified; (2) that the subscribers' subscription for shares be accepted and shares be allotted and issued for agreed consideration, with share certificates executed per the Memorandum of Incorporation; (3) that the registered office be and is hereby established at 17 Buchanan Square, 161 Sir Lowry Road, Cape Town, 8001; (4) that [Director] be appointed sole Director, [Company Secretary] Company Secretary, and [CA(SA)] Accounting Officer; (5) that the Director be authorized to open bank accounts and execute documents incidental to trading.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form CoR 9.1 online proposing up to three alternative names in order of preference; select entity type 'Private Company (Pty) Ltd' and describe the fabless semiconductor design and IP licensing business; upon approval, the name is reserved for six months pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 (Name Reservation Application)
Certified copies of identity documents or passports of incorporating shareholders
Consent letter for use of a name (if the requested name is not the applicant's own)
Disclosure of any registered trademarks conflicting with the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, file a revised CoR 9.1 with materially distinct names or submit representations to the CIPC Companies Tribunal under s. 160 of the Companies Act for an order overriding the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal; CIPC head office, Pretoria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CoR 14.1 and attach the signed MOI and required consents; pay the prescribed filing fee electronically; CIPC verifies the registration and issues the Certificate of Incorporation together with a company registration number. The company acquires juristic personality from the date and time stated on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Memorandum of Incorporation signed by each incorporator (with ISIC 2610 commercial object clause)
Name reservation approval letter (CoR 9.1 outcome)
Form CoR 21.5 (Consent to Act as Director) executed by each proposed director
Certified identity documents of directors and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any CIPC requisition through e-Services within the prescribed period, amend the defective fields or attachments, and re-lodge; if the application is rejected a second time, escalate via the CIPC contact centre and obtain a written requisition log before re-filing a fresh CoR 14.1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Accounting Officer and Independent Reviewer
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC; Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors (IRBA); South African Institute of Chartered Accountants (SAICA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate the company's Public Interest Score under Companies Regulation 26; for a private fabless design company with a score below 350, appoint a registered accounting officer and, where required by the MOI or by regulation, an independent reviewer; record appointments by written board resolution and file Form CoR 30.1 where applicable.
required_dossiers: Public Interest Score calculation worksheet
Form CoR 30.1 (Notice of Appointment of Auditor/Reviewed) if the score threshold is met
Signed board resolution appointing the accounting officer
IRBA/SAICA registration particulars of the appointee
Independence declaration from the accounting officer/reviewer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Interest Score subsequently exceeds 350, appoint a registered auditor and file the amended notice with CIPC within 40 business days to avoid a compliance notice under Companies Regulation 32.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Employer Registration with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Income Tax, Value-Added Tax (if taxable turnover exceeds or is projected to exceed R1 million per annum), Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Skills Development Levy (SDL) via SARS eFiling within 60 days after incorporation; obtain a tax registration number and complete the first provisional income tax return where applicable.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
SARS Income Tax registration form (IT120) or eFiling electronic equivalent
Bank account confirmation on bank letterhead
Certified identity documents of directors
Projected turnover and financial forecast supporting VAT registration
CSD or B-BBEE affidavit (if contracting with public sector clients)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a Notice of Objection under s. 104 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 if SARS does not finalise the registration within 21 business days; alternatively, apply for a suspension of penalties under s. 89 of that Act while the registration query is being resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Compensation Fund and Workplace Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour - Compensation Fund (CF); local fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as an employer under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993 (COIDA) within seven days of engaging the first employee; declare the workplace premises at the registered office; obtain a letter of good standing and ensure the premises meet SANS 10400 fire-safety and OHSA requirements before business commencement.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
Compensation Fund employer registration form (W.As. 2)
Estimated annual remuneration schedule for employees
Certificate of Occupancy / lease agreement of the registered office
Electrical Certificate of Compliance (SANS 10142-1)
Fire-safety compliance certificate from the local fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration is permitted upon submission of a sworn affidavit explaining the delay and payment of any minimal administrative penalty; if the fire or electrical certificate is non-compliant, retain a qualified technician to rectify defects and re-inspect before the Compensation Fund issues the letter of good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic); National Regulator for Compulsory Specification (NRCS); International Trade Administration Commission (ITAC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Fabless Semiconductor Design Centre Registration (no factory/foundry licence required); ITAC Export Control Permit for transfers of dual-use semiconductor IP and technology under the ITAC Act 71 of 2002; NRCS Letter of Authority (Compulsory Specification VC 8059) if hardware prototypes are imported or placed on the South African market.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - EIA Exemption/Registration Tier under the 2014 EIA Regulations (Listing Notices 1, 2 and 3); pure office-based fabless design is excluded from formal EIA, but a Basic Assessment is triggered where the development footprint exceeds 2,000 m² or the premises fall within a sensitive environmental zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated industrial point-source emissions for fabless design activity; compliance with municipal wastewater and stormwater bylaws, SANS 10400-A ventilation requirements, and the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 (NEM:WA) for the classification, storage, and disposal of e-waste and prototype IC samples by a licensed carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate under SANS 10400 Part T issued by the local fire authority; occupational clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 with a documented risk assessment (Regulation 3) and first-aid equipment certification; electrical certificate of compliance (SANS 10142-1) for the leased premises; no structural load inspection is required for standard commercial office occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first register as a taxpayer with SARS via eFiling, using the IT77 (company registration) form or outsourcing to a registered tax practitioner. Required supporting documents include the Memorandum of Incorporation, proof of registered office address in South Africa, directors' particulars, and evidence of appointment of a resident public officer. SARS issues an income tax reference number and, where relevant, a VAT vendor number after verifying the entity's constitutional documents and operational presence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the South African Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, no check-the-box pass-through election is available for a (Pty) Ltd; the entity is taxed at corporate level. Where hybrid or cross-border mismatch arrangements exist, elections are limited to those prescribed under the OECD BEPS Action 2 recommendations as domesticated in Section 8I and 8J for hybrid instruments; no elective fiscal consolidation or group relief is available beyond Section 14(1) companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration threshold: ZAR 1,000,000 on aggregate taxable supplies over any 12-month rolling period; voluntary registration permitted from ZAR 50,000 where a continuing business exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS operates a structured e-invoicing framework under the VAT Act and the Customs and Excise Act. Vendor invoices must contain prescribed particulars (e.g., VAT vendor number, invoice number, supply date, consideration). Real-time fiscal clearance is not yet mandatory for domestic B2B invoices; however, all VAT returns are filed electronically via eFiling, and for exported goods, the Customs Clearing House (SAD500) processes declarations electronically through SARS' external customs module. Digital stamping is not generally required, but the SARS eFiling channel is the sole recognised submission portal for tax and customs declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Section 11 of the VAT Act applies to (a) the supply of movable goods exported by the vendor, or by the purchaser under the vendor's authority, under a sale agreement, to a destination outside South Africa; and (b) the supply of services physically performed outside South Africa, or for the direct benefit of non-residents who are outside South Africa at the time of supply (subject to circular  measurable use and enjoyment rules). A fabless semiconductor design entity can claim zero-rating on exports of IP licences and design IP core deliverables only where the recipient is a non-resident and the contract evidences a supply of services connected to foreign jurisdiction without any use in South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 – Bill 1, Export Declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods (or, for services, a signed contractual agreement explicitly transferring the IP/licence outside South Africa)
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of foreign currency payment received in South African banking channel
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may audit export zero-rating claims under Section 74 of the VAT Act and the Customs Control Act. Non-compliance, including failure to retain the prescribed documentation, furnishing false export declarations, or failure to repatriate foreign consideration within the exchange-control deadline, triggers a full VAT clawback plus interest from the date of the original zero-rated supply. Criminal penalties include a fine or imprisonment of up to five years for intentional evasion; civil understatement penalties under Chapter 16 of the Tax Administration Act (up to 200% of a repayment or excessive claim) apply. SARS also has four-year prescription extended to five years where fraud or misrepresentation is proven.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the delegated authority of the Minister of Finance conferred by the Currency and Exchanges Act, No. 9 of 1933, and the Exchange Control Regulations promulgated thereunder. The National Treasury retains policy oversight; Authorized Dealers (registered commercial banks) execute day-to-day exchange-control decisions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is administratively convertible: current account items (trade in services, IP royalties, invoiced export receipts, bona fide operational payments) are freely transferable through an Authorized Dealer with proper supporting documentation, while capital account flows (non-resident equity subscriptions, disinvestments, foreign borrowings, capital repatriations) require either prior FinSurv approval or completion of regulated declarations. Profit and dividend remittance is lawful once the Authorized Dealer verifies 'own funds' (paid-up share capital plus accumulated realized profits) on Form A1; the statutory 20% dividend withholding tax (or treaty-reduced rate) must be withheld for non-resident shareholders. Cross-border IP royalty outflows are subject to a 15% withholding tax unless a double tax treaty reduces the rate, together with SARS section 23D deductibility limits and section 31 transfer-pricing scrutiny. Practical hurdles include the 180-day export receipt and 30-day surrender requirements, the FIC 5% beneficial-ownership disclosure duties, the requirement that the company maintain a physical South African registered office and a local authorized signatory, and the prohibition on speculative open FX positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (section 26, Companies Act 2008) including revenue-band declaration; Tier 1 fee ZAR 100 applicable to annual turnover below ZAR 10 million
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation; the anniversary date, not the financial year-end, determines the filing window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty of ZAR 50; failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off (deregistration) under section 82 of the Companies Act 2008, with company assets vesting in the State upon dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register annual confirmation and update (section 51, Companies Act 2008 as amended by the General Laws Amendment Act 2022 and CIPC Directive 4 of 2022); separate CIPC e-filing fee ZAR 50
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in conjunction with the CIPC Annual Return (incorporation anniversary); any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with CIPC within 7 business days after the company becomes aware of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate UBO information is a criminal offence under the amended Companies Act; CIPC may issue a compliance notice, and persistent default supports administrative strike-off of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) - preparation, board approval, audit or independent review, and on-site retention (sections 29-33, Companies Act 2008)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors (approval authority); CIPC (filing required only for public-interest companies or where the MOI or CIPC prescribes filing); AFS retained at the registered office for all private companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the relevant financial year; audit or independent review must be completed before board approval and before delivery to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors commit an offence under section 33 if AFS are not approved and retained within 6 months of financial year-end; CIPC compliance notice and potential fine, with cumulative default supporting deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Public Interest Score (PIS) annual computation and audit exemption substantiation (Companies Regulations 2011, regulations 26-28)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC and the external accounting professional (record must substantiate the audit or independent-review exemption claimed on the AFS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Computed as at each financial year-end and retained with the AFS working papers for 7 years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective PIS or false exemption claim renders the AFS non-compliant; CIPC may require a retroactive statutory audit at company cost, and directors may face compliance penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies where: (1) the Public Interest Score (PIS) at financial year-end is 350 or more; (2) the PIS is between 100 and 349 and the AFS were internally compiled by directors or prescribed officers rather than by an independent accounting professional; (3) the company holds assets in a fiduciary capacity with aggregate value exceeding ZAR 5 million; (4) the company is a public, state-owned, or listed company; or (5) the MOI or a shareholder resolution requires an audit. A fabless semiconductor design and IP-licensing private company with PIS below 100 is exempt from audit and independent review if the AFS are externally compiled.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (recognised as the applicable South African GAAP framework under section 29, Companies Act 2008) for private companies not in the public interest; full IFRS for public-interest entities and where otherwise required by the MOI or regulators

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CIPC Annual Return contains the mandatory annual beneficial-ownership declaration; the company must maintain a standing UBO register at its registered office, reconstructing it where necessary from share-transfer records. Share transfers and other UBO changes, including indirect control through trusts or partnerships and acquisitions of 5% or more of issued shares, must be recorded in the register and e-filed with CIPC within 7 business days of the company becoming aware of the change. The annual return confirmation is signed by an authorised director or Company Secretary and certifies the UBO register as complete and accurate as at the anniversary date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Prescribed Officers
Register of Directors' Interests in Securities

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 per annum (full statutory audit); USD 1,200 - 3,500 per annum (independent review); USD 600 - 1,500 per annum (external AFS compilation only)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% normal corporate income tax for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; the section 11D R&D incentive grants an additional 50% deduction (150% total) for approved R&D expenditure; section 12C accelerated depreciation applies to qualifying movable manufacturing assets; assessed losses are carried forward indefinitely, subject to the 80% taxable-income set-off cap applicable for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2020.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Companies Income Tax Return, filed through SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year; provisional estimates impose intermediate payment dates before and at year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact Pty Ltd registration number; non-resident shareholders are not recorded on the company's income tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS taxpayer reference number and branch code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the South African branch tax reference; a non-resident company trading through a permanent establishment in South Africa files under a separate branch profile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial year-end, basis period, and assessment number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the 12-month period or approved accounting period; no non-resident-specific entry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and ISIC classification (ISIC 2610 / NAICS 334413 – fabless semiconductor design and IP core licensing)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the actual South African trade; passive offshore royalty recipients should not be reported as the trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income: sales, IP royalties, licence fees, and other amounts accrued to the company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are not generally taxable on mere local revenue unless sourced in South Africa; the Pty Ltd must disclose all worldwide income.
Only statutory exemptions may be deducted; treaty-related exempt income must be supported by a Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions, including section 11D R&D deduction, amortisation, and operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches may deduct expenses connected with South African-source income under section 25B/35A rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward and current-year assessed loss computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply section 20 set-off rules; a non-resident branch may only use losses attributable to the South African trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, normal tax at 27%, and prepayments/provisional tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch profits are remitted without dividend tax; branch remittance tax does not apply in South Africa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers administrative non-compliance penalties under the Tax Administration Act 2011 (up to ZAR 1,000 per month for smaller entities and higher tariffs for large businesses), default assessments, and prescribed-rate interest. A failed tax position attracts an understatement penalty of 25% (substantial understatement), 50% (reasonable care failure), 75% (no reasonable grounds), or 150% (intentional evasion).
